brief.desc: Bearish, 40/100. Gold is in a falling trend caught between a Fed still hiking into an oil shock and two weeks of easing real yields it has barely rallied on. GLD sits 25% below its 52-week high, 4.8% lower over 20 days and below both its 50- and 200-day averages.
brief.yr: GLD closed Friday October 16 at 382.01, down 0.18%, in a 380.90 to 384.88 range, after a 1.79% gain on Thursday; spot ended at 4,165.50, down 0.13%. Futures printed +0.40% to 4,186.70 only because Thursday's late rally fell after the 1:30 PM settle; over two days all instruments are up roughly 1.5 to 1.9%. The move came from rates and the dollar: the Treasury 10-year real yield fell to 2.74%, 19bp off its September 30 peak, and DXY slipped to 101.84 after Fed Chair Warsh avoided signalling an October hike. GLD has still not escaped the 373 to 385 range it has held since the September 28 break.
brief.to: Base cases are a grind lower toward 4,000 futures (40%) if December hike odds hold and real yields rebound above 2.85%, or a 4,100 to 4,250 range into the October 28 FOMC (40%); a real-yield breakdown to 4,400 carries 20%. With the Fed in blackout from October 17, the week's catalysts are the October 21 20-year auction, October 22 jobless claims and October 23 flash PMIs, UMich inflation expectations and the CFTC positioning report. This view flips bullish if the 10-year TIPS real yield closes below 2.60%.

brief.why: The regime is an inflation-driven tightening cycle, and gold is not hedging it well. September CPI ran 3.7% year on year with +0.6% month on month, and PPI rose 1.3% on the month, both led by oil as attacks near Hormuz hold Brent near 105 dollars. The Fed hiked in September. A move to 3.75-4.00% with headline CPI at 3.7% leaves the real policy rate barely positive, so the market prices more, and the 10-year nominal at 5.09% and real at 2.74% carry that. Breakevens stuck at 2.35% say bonds believe the Fed will win, which is the bearish mix for gold: the inflation shows up in real rates, not in breakevens. The past two weeks loosened this. Real yields fell 19bp from September 30 on AI-capex debt worries and because Warsh did not validate an October move, yet GLD gained only about 0.3% over the same span. A market that cannot rally on 19bp of real-yield relief is still being sold into, and the obvious seller is positioning: managed money is still net long 107 thousand contracts against 17.7 thousand shorts, leftover longs from a market 25% below its January high, and they are bleeding out. Underneath, central-bank buying has slowed to 170 tonnes year to date through August, with Turkey and Russia net sellers. Record Q3 ETF inflows of 31 billion dollars are the main counterweight, but they came while GLD fell, which suggests dip-buying that is now underwater.
brief.cons: Commentary has turned constructive on falling yields and a softer dollar, geopolitics and record ETF inflows. That is premature: the bounce is a rates trade, not a gold-specific one, and it rests on a rate path that has not changed. Rate odds are noisy across outlets, with an October hold put at roughly 66% to 85% and a December hike at roughly 63% to 89%, but December is priced as more likely than not either way. The crowded side is still long, with managed money's long-to-short ratio near 7 to 1, so the bearish call is not crowded. The risk to it is the reverse: if ETF dip-buyers are a durable new holder base rather than tourists, the liquidation runs out of fuel near 375 on GLD.
fals: Soften: GLD closes above its 50-day moving average of 397.18 before the October 28 FOMC; I would move to neutral.

Invert: the Treasury 10-year real yield closes below 2.60%, below every print since September 10, meaning the December hike is priced out; I would go bullish. Watch the daily Treasury post, with the October 28 FOMC as the latest test.

Weak joint: the call assumes managed-money longs keep liquidating and that Q3's record ETF inflows are not continuing into October. No October ETF flow data has been seen; WGC data runs only to October 9. The October 23 COT report and early-November WGC flows settle it.
